title: write-before-ioctl for KEY_IMPORT avoids large on-stack allocation
description: Why it is right: KEY_IMPORT does not embed key bytes in the ioctl struct. Instead the caller writes raw key bytes to the fd, then the ioctl reads op.keylen bytes from inbuf. The alternative — a struct with an 8192-byte key[] array — would land that 8KB allocation on the kernel stack on every KEY_IMPORT call regardless of actual key size (EC P-256 is 32 bytes). The kernel stack frame guideline is ~1KB; an 8192-byte stack frame is a hard violation that can silently corrupt adjacent frames on stack-limited configs (4KB stacks on some embedded targets) or under deep call chains. inbuf is heap-allocated to exactly what the key requires, zeroed, and freed after import. What a reviewer might incorrectly suggest: 'just embed key[] in the ioctl struct for simplicity; 8KB is fine.' The kernel disagrees: scripts/checkpatch.pl warns on stack frames > 512 bytes, and some architectures enforce 4KB total stack depth.
